review.summary: The packet appears to conflict with state ADU law (Gov. Code §§ 66310-66342) in 17 places. The most serious are the owner-occupancy requirement for ADUs, the ADU deed restriction, HOA and coastal approval as prescreen conditions, unit-count limits, and design standards applied to all units. This is a screening against the loaded sources only, not legal advice. Some items depend on whether a unit is a § 66323 unit, and the coastal item depends on San Clemente's Local Coastal Program, which the loaded sources do not cover.

issues.rule: § 17.28.270 E.7.b: ADUs permitted on or after Jan 1, 2025 are subject to owner occupancy.
issues.conflict: State law bars owner-occupancy requirements for ADUs. The only exception is an ADU sold to a qualified buyer under § 66341(c)(3).
issues.quote: a local agency cannot impose an owner-occupancy requirement on any other ADU

issues.rule: Deed restriction on ADUs recorded before a building permit issues and running with the land (also required as a submittal step).
issues.conflict: HCD says a local agency likely cannot impose a deed restriction on an ADU. A JADU deed restriction limited to the JADU-law items is permitted. Fix: apply it to JADUs only.
issues.quote: A local agency cannot impose a deed restriction on an ADU.

issues.rule: Ownership: ADU/JADU may not be sold separately.
issues.conflict: A blanket ban on separate sale appears to ignore the mandated § 66341 exception for ADUs built by a qualified nonprofit and sold to a qualified buyer. Fix: add that exception. Separate sale as condominiums under § 66342 is optional.
issues.quote: Allowing ADUs to be sold separately if they meet the requirements of Government Code section 66341 is mandated by the statute

issues.rule: Submittal step: HOA approval if applicable, and evidence of HOA approval required for the City ADU prescreen.
issues.conflict: HCD says HOA review or approval cannot be part of the ministerial ADU process. Making it a precondition to processing likely violates state law. Fix: delete it and leave HOA matters to the applicant.
issues.quote: third party reviews by an HOA or their representatives or agents would violate State ADU Law.

issues.rule: City ADU prescreen requires evidence of Coastal approval before building permit processing (Coastal Commission approval required in the Coastal Zone).
issues.conflict: State law runs the coastal development permit review concurrently with the ADU review rather than requiring it first. Making it a prerequisite appears to conflict, subject to the Coastal Act and the LCP, which the loaded sources do not cover. Fix: process the two concurrently.
issues.quote: The process to approve or deny a coastal development permit application shall happen concurrently with the process to approve or deny an application for an ADU

issues.rule: Quantity (single-family lot): one JADU plus one detached or attached ADU.
issues.conflict: State law requires allowing a converted ADU, a JADU, and a new detached ADU together on a single-family lot. The packet's one-ADU limit appears too restrictive.
issues.quote: on single-family lots, local agencies must allow at least one ADU constructed from existing space, one JADU, and one newly constructed detached ADU.

issues.rule: Quantity (multifamily): up to two detached ADUs.
issues.conflict: On a lot with an existing multifamily dwelling, state law allows up to eight detached ADUs, capped at the number of existing units. Two is the number for a proposed multifamily dwelling.
issues.quote: or up to eight detached ADUs are allowed on a lot with an existing multifamily dwelling, not to exceed the number of existing units on the lot.

issues.rule: Front setback: no closer to the front line than the primary dwelling's living area (in addition to the zone front setback).
issues.conflict: Front setbacks cannot preclude an ADU of at least 800 sq ft, and § 66323 detached ADUs may sit in the front setback. This added build-line rule appears likely to violate that.
issues.quote: front yard setbacks cannot preclude an ADU of at least 800 square feet from being built on the property

issues.rule: Separation from primary building: 5 feet (including eaves).
issues.conflict: State law bars minimum-distance requirements that unreasonably restrict ADUs unless required by the Building or Fire Code. A flat 5-foot rule appears likely to conflict, especially for § 66323 units. Fix: defer to building and fire code separation.
issues.quote: Minimum distance or other requirements may not be applied if they would unreasonably restrict the creation of ADUs

issues.rule: Height limits list only 16 ft detached and 18 ft near transit (plus 2 ft for roof pitch).
issues.conflict: The packet omits the required 18-foot allowance for a detached ADU on a lot with an existing or proposed multifamily, multistory dwelling.
issues.quote: 18 feet height on a lot with an existing or proposed multifamily, multistory dwelling

issues.rule: Parking: exemption only for a 'posted' car-share location within one block.
issues.conflict: State law exempts an ADU whenever a car share vehicle is located within one block. The added 'posted' condition narrows the exemption.
issues.quote: When there is a car share vehicle located within one block of the ADU.

issues.conflict: State law caps parking at one space per unit or per bedroom, whichever is less. A studio or efficiency unit with no bedroom likely cannot be required to provide a space. Fix: add the bedroom cap.
issues.quote: Parking requirements for accessory dwelling units shall not exceed one parking space per accessory dwelling unit or per bedroom, whichever is less.

issues.rule: Efficiency unit minimum: 220 sq ft plus 100 sq ft per occupant beyond two.
issues.conflict: The ordinance cannot set a minimum size that prohibits efficiency units, which may be as small as 150 sq ft. The 220 sq ft minimum appears too high.
issues.quote: An efficiency unit may be as small as 150 square feet in floor area (HSC, § 17958.1).

issues.rule: § 17.28.270 F.7 architecture: materials, colors, windows and doors must match the primary dwelling; roof slope must match; down-lights only; interior at least 10 ft wide; 7 ft walls.
issues.conflict: Standards must be objective, and 'match' is open to interpretation unless it is defined by measurable criteria. These design and size rules also cannot be applied to § 66323 units. A 10-ft minimum interior width may unreasonably restrict small units. Fix: use measurable criteria and exempt § 66323 units.
issues.quote: Subjective standards require independent judgement and are open to multiple interpretations.

issues.rule: Owner occupancy: JADU requires owner occupancy.
issues.conflict: State law requires owner occupancy only when the JADU shares sanitation facilities with the primary structure. Fix: limit the requirement to shared-sanitation JADUs.
issues.quote: If the JADU does not have shared sanitation facilities, owner occupancy will not be required (Gov. Code, § 66333, subd. (b)).

issues.rule: Fees: § 17.28.270 D.4.a, no impact fee for ADUs 'under 750 sq ft'.
issues.conflict: State law bars impact fees for ADUs of 750 sq ft or less, so an ADU of exactly 750 sq ft is exempt. 'Under 750' appears to charge the 750 sq ft case.
issues.quote: to prohibit impact fees on the development of an ADU that has 750 square feet of interior livable space or less

issues.rule: § 17.28.270 H: ADUs not meeting objective standards may be allowed with an Architectural Permit.
issues.conflict: This is likely acceptable only as an optional extra path. If it is used to deny or delay ADUs that fail local standards, it would be a discretionary process, which state law bars. Fix: state that it is optional and that state-mandated approvals are unconditional.
issues.quote: This approval process shall not include discretionary processes, provisions, or requirements except as provided in Government Code section

issues.rule: Review time: '60 days when a complete application is submitted.'
issues.conflict: The 60-day statement alone appears incomplete. State law also requires a written completeness determination within 15 business days, a list of any deficiencies, and an appeal process. The packet does not cover these (not covered by loaded sources).
issues.quote: provide written notice of the determination not later than 15 business days after the permitting agency received the application

matches.matched_issue: Quantity (multifamily): up to two detached ADUs.: state law allows up to eight detached ADUs, capped at number of existing units.
